rationale: The exact corrected decision properly leaves whole-order status unresolved; its rationale now accurately distinguishes partial/conditional displacement from complete revocation. EO 10582 §§1–5, 19 FR 8723 and 8725 (raw PDF pp.1 and 3; intervening p.2 is contents). Section 2 defines foreign content and bid-price differentials. Section 3 preserves particular agency choices; §4 directs conforming procurement regulations; §5 limits temporal application, permits specified agency determinations and requires a written presidential report within 30 days of each determination. Sections 4–5 are potential commands that require provision-level treatment; a partial inconsistency clause does not dispose of all of them. EO 14005 §14(b), 86 FR 7478 (PDF p.4), supersedes EO 10582 only 'to the extent that they are inconsistent with this order.' Section 14(a)'s outright revocation concerns different listed orders. EO 13881 §3, also supplied in the reviewed source set, additionally conditions revocation of only EO 10582 §§2(a),2(c) on issuance of a final rule; its full text does not revoke §§1–5 wholesale. EO 10582 §§3,5 contain substantive exceptions and reporting machinery. The current operation of the surviving provisions, later regulations and conditional rule issuance remains unresolved in this bounded packet. Mere passage of the reporting period or newer procurement policy cannot prove complete cessation. EO 14148's full list omits EO 14005 and EO 10582. It supplies neither whole-order revocation nor an affirmative answer about surviving procurement provisions.
